Nezahat Gökyiğit Park, Istanbul | genus = Limonium | species =sinuatum | authority = ([[Carl Linnaeus|L.]]) [[Philip Miller|Mill.]] }} '''''Limonium sinuatum''''', commonly known as '''wavyleaf sea lavender''', statice, sea lavender, notch leaf marsh rosemary, sea pink,{{cite web|url=http://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/080c0106-040c-4508-8300-0b0a06060e01/media/Html/Limonium_sinuatum.htm |title=Factsheet - Limonium sinuatum |accessdate=2015-01-12 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150622111144/http://keyserver.lucidcentral.org/weeds/data/080c0106-040c-4508-8300-0b0a06060e01/media/Html/Limonium_sinuatum.htm |archivedate=2015-06-22 }}{{Cite web | url=http://www.egmontseeds.co.nz/flowers/statice-pacific-mix |title = Statice Pacific Mix : Egmont Seed Company LTD, Online seed sales}} is a Mediterranean plant species in the family [[Plumbaginaceae]] known for its papery flowers that can be used in dried arrangements. It is native to the whole [[Mediterranean Basin]].{{cite web |title=Limonium sinuatum |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/03_055_04_Limonium.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=16 July 2022}} It usually grows up in sandy grounds. ==Description== It is a short-lived perennial plant, and is often treated as an annual. The leaves are pinnate, lobed, and lance-shaped – up to {{convert|10|cm|in|abbr=on}} long. All parts are downy. The winged flower stems appear in summer, and are about {{convert|70|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall. The flowers present in short, papery clusters in colours ranging from white to pink, purple, and yellow. It has been known to become invasive.{{cite book|title=Flora - The Gardener's Bible|date=2013|publisher=David Bateman Ltd|location=New Zealand|isbn=978-1-74048-017-8|page=821}} Limonium sinuatum 04 ies.jpg|''Limonium sinuatum'' Limonium sinuatum 01 ies.jpg|''Limonium sinuatum'' Yellow Statice flowers, close up from side.JPG|Yellow statice flowers, close up from side Yellow Statice flowers, close up from top.JPG|Yellow statice flowers, close up from top Limonium sinatum 'Midnight Blue' (Plumbagnaceae) flower.JPG|''Limonium sinatum'' 'Midnight Blue' ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q542644}} [[Category:Limonium|sinuatum]] [[Category:Garden plants of Europe]] [[Category:Drought-tolerant plants]] [[Category:Flora of Lebanon]] [[Category:Taxa named by Philip Miller]] [[Category:Flora of Malta]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]]
